skill.name: dast-ffuf
skill.description: Guides authorized ffuf web fuzzing for directory discovery, parameter testing, virtual host enumeration, filtering, recursion, output review, and CI security checks.
skill.summary: Plan and refine authorized ffuf scans with practical filters, rate limits, and result handling.
skill.author: AgentSecOps

security_audit.summary: Most static hits are false positives from Markdown syntax, reference links, and labeled security examples. The CI template has a critical supply-chain risk because it pipes an unpinned remote script into Bash. The skill also provides high-impact credential fuzzing and reconnaissance workflows that require explicit authorization.

remediation.issue: The CI template executes a mutable remote installer with curl piped directly to Bash.
remediation.suggestion: Download a version-pinned release, verify its checksum or signature, and execute the verified local file as a separate step.

remediation.issue: Authentication workflows can enumerate users and test password combinations.
remediation.suggestion: Require written authorization, a defined account scope, lockout monitoring, strict rate limits, and test credentials before generating these workflows.

remediation.issue: The workflow advises downloading exposed backup and sensitive files.
remediation.suggestion: Default to metadata-only validation, minimize collection, encrypt approved evidence, and document retention and deletion requirements.

content.user_title: Plan Authorized Web Fuzzing with ffuf
content.value_statement: Web fuzzing creates noisy results and legal exposure when scope, filters, and rate limits are unclear. This skill produces authorized ffuf workflows with focused discovery, filtering, output, and CI guidance.
actual_capabilities: Plans directory and file discovery with wordlists, extensions, recursion, and response-code matching.
Configures GET, form, and JSON parameter fuzzing for authorized application testing.
Guides virtual host discovery through Host header fuzzing and response-size filtering.
Explains clusterbomb, pitchfork, and sniper modes for one or multiple wordlists.
Tunes status, size, word, line, regex, delay, and concurrency filters.
Provides output, troubleshooting, OWASP mapping, and CI integration examples.
limitations: Requires ffuf, suitable wordlists, network access, and permission to test the target.
Cannot verify authorization, target ownership, legal scope, or program rules.
Cannot confirm vulnerabilities without manual review and independent validation.
Credential fuzzing can trigger lockouts, alerts, service impact, or policy violations.

use_cases.title: Map Staging Content
use_cases.description: Create a rate-limited directory and file discovery plan for an owned staging application.

use_cases.title: Test Authorized Parameters
use_cases.description: Build focused GET or POST parameter tests with filters that reduce baseline noise.

use_cases.title: Add Controlled DAST Checks
use_cases.description: Design a repeatable CI check that records ffuf results and flags exposed sensitive paths.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Directory Discovery
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a basic ffuf plan for [authorized target] using [wordlist]. Use low concurrency, explain response filters, and save reviewable results.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for an owned staging host

prompt_templates.title: Focused Parameter Testing
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan authorized fuzzing for [endpoint] and [parameter location]. Include a baseline request, payload category, matching rules, rate limits, and manual validation steps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate GET or POST parameter assessment

prompt_templates.title: Virtual Host Assessment
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a scoped virtual host discovery workflow for [base domain]. Explain calibration, false-positive reduction, DNS validation, request limits, and evidence handling.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced infrastructure discovery within a defined scope

prompt_templates.title: Controlled CI Integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a CI ffuf check for [staging URL]. Pin dependencies, avoid remote pipe execution, set failure criteria, protect artifacts, and limit requests.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced repeatable DAST testing in CI

output_examples.input: Plan low-impact directory discovery for an authorized staging host.
output: Scope: one staging host with a written testing window.
Method: establish a baseline, use a small wordlist, and limit concurrency.
Review: group unusual status and size results before manual validation.

output_examples.input: Reduce false positives after every path returns a successful response.
output: Baseline: request random nonexistent paths and record common response sizes.
Filtering: exclude the stable wildcard signature and keep meaningful deviations.
Validation: repeat selected results and compare content before reporting.

output_examples.input: Add ffuf to a staging security pipeline.
output: Dependency control: install a pinned ffuf release from a verified artifact.
Execution control: use a narrow wordlist, fixed scope, and request limits.
Evidence control: retain sanitized results and fail only on validated policy conditions.

best_practices: Obtain written authorization and define hosts, paths, methods, credentials, timing, and request limits before testing.
Start with small wordlists and low concurrency, then expand only after reviewing target stability and baseline responses.
Validate findings manually and protect result files because responses may contain credentials or personal data.
anti_patterns: Do not scan public or third-party targets without explicit written permission.
Do not use large credential lists against production authentication endpoints.
Do not pipe remote installers into a shell or depend on mutable branches in CI.

faq.question: Does this skill install ffuf?
faq.answer: No. It provides installation guidance, but you must install and verify ffuf in your environment.

faq.question: Can it test any public website?
faq.answer: No. Test only systems covered by written authorization, a bug bounty scope, or documented ownership.

faq.question: Which ffuf modes are covered?
faq.answer: It covers standard single-wordlist use plus clusterbomb, pitchfork, and sniper workflows.

faq.question: How does it reduce false positives?
faq.answer: It explains auto-calibration and filters for status, size, words, lines, and regular expressions.

faq.question: Does it confirm vulnerabilities automatically?
faq.answer: No. Results identify response differences and exposed content that require manual validation.

faq.question: Can it support CI pipelines?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a staging-oriented pattern for saved results, policy checks, and report artifacts.
